title: Fixed-Key Probabilities for Non-Plateau Characteristics
summary: Existing fixed-key analysis covers only plateau characteristics; the open task is to derive meaningful fixed-key probability expressions for a large family of non-plateau characteristics.

formal_statement.body: Generalize fixed-key differential analysis from plateau characteristics, currently covered only when every internal S-box differential is super-planar, to non-plateau characteristics without that strong structure. For S-boxes with differential uniformity at most $4$, this super-planarity condition is equivalent to requiring every internal S-box to be active. Derive meaningful expressions for the fixed-key probabilities of a large family of non-plateau characteristics while jointly incorporating the S-boxes' differential properties and Walsh spectra; the quasi-differential framework is a promising avenue.

scope.domain: Fixed-key differential cryptanalysis of lightweight symmetric designs, focusing on S-box characteristics beyond the plateau case.
assumptions: S-boxes have differential uniformity at most 4.
parameters: Non-plateau characteristics: the target family for generalized fixed-key analysis
S-box differential properties: information to be incorporated into the probability expressions
Walsh spectra: additional spectral information required for the non-plateau case
scope.unresolved_remainder: Derive meaningful expressions for the fixed-key probabilities of a large family of non-plateau characteristics, jointly incorporating the S-boxes' differential properties and Walsh spectra.

citations.label: Understanding Unexpected Fixed-Key Differential Behaviours: How to Avoid Major Weaknesses in Lightweight Designs

progress.summary: The source presents this as a major limitation of the current analysis, which is restricted to super-planar internal S-box differentials and hence plateau characteristics. It identifies the quasi-differential framework as a promising route, while noting that useful expressions remain challenging because both differential properties and Walsh spectra are involved.
citation_labels: Anne Canteaut et al., Understanding Unexpected Fixed-Key Differential Behaviours: How to Avoid Major Weaknesses in Lightweight Designs
